purpose: Classify the Casoratian transport theorem, the telescoping q-Apéry product, and the finite source replay without promoting a routine recurrence invariant into a novelty or irrationality claim.

classification.standard_mechanism: the discrete Wronskian of two solutions of one scalar second-order recurrence satisfies a first-order multiplicative recurrence; substituting the q-Apéry coefficients makes the product telescope
classification.attribution: Attribute the q-Apéry sequences and common recurrence to Tewodros Amdeberhan and Doron Zeilberger. Describe the determinant transport as the standard discrete Abel--Liouville or Casoratian identity. Present the closed product and the 3/2 valuation shear as elementary consequences derived from the published coefficients, with the defining-sum match verified only over the declared finite range.
classification.mathematical_interest: The abstract theorem is routine. The source-specific value is diagnostic: the exact nonzero product shows that adjacent proportionality is not the obstruction at 3/2, while its opposite 2-adic and 3-adic valuations expose why the raw determinant does not provide simultaneous local gain.
classification.reusable_scope: Any pair of solutions of a scalar second-order linear difference equation with nonzero leading coefficient; a nonzero seed and nonzero transport factors rule out adjacent proportionality on the interval of definition.
classification.why_it_matters: It cheaply retires a false collapse explanation before expensive Padé or lattice work. For this programme it redirects attention to denominator clearing, primitive height, analytic remainder, and congruence-constrained selection without claiming any of those obligations are solved.

primary_sources.title: q-Apéry Irrationality Proofs by q-WZ Pairs
primary_sources.author: Tewodros Amdeberhan and Doron Zeilberger
primary_sources.exact_anchor: §0 (pp. 1-2) attributes q-harmonic irrationality work to Erdős and Borwein; §§1.5-1.6 define the second-order operator L, prove both sequences solve L, subtract their recurrences, and derive the successive-approximant estimate (1.6.4).
primary_sources.supports: The source identity, recurrence coefficients, initial data, and direct q-Apéry attribution. It is also the closest antecedent to the local Casoratian calculation.
primary_sources.does_not_support: An all-index statement at rational q=3/2 after denominator clearing, the exact closed product as a separately stated theorem, the card's valuation shear, or irrationality at 3/2.

mechanism_comparison.Casoratian: The determinant $u_{n+1}v_n-u_nv_{n+1}$ is the standard discrete analogue of the Wronskian.
mechanism_comparison.discrete_Abel_Liouville_identity: For $A_nw_{n+2}+B_nw_{n+1}+C_nw_n=0$, direct elimination gives $W_{n+1}=(C_n/A_n)W_n$ under the card's sign convention.
mechanism_comparison.q_apery_specialization: Substitution of the published coefficients turns the transport product into a telescoping ratio; the closed form is source-specific but elementary once the recurrence and seed are granted.
mechanism_comparison.finite_source_replay: Exact symbolic checks through n=4 verify that the paper's defining sums instantiate the recurrence and closed form over that range. They do not prove the source specialization for every n.

disconfirmation_search.result: The search confirms that Casoratian/discrete Wronskian is established terminology and that the multiplicative transport is the discrete Abel--Liouville mechanism. The primary q-Apéry paper already contains the shared recurrence and a subtraction argument for successive approximants. No basis remains for a new general theorem claim.
disconfirmation_search.boundary: The bounded search did not establish whether the exact telescoped product has appeared elsewhere. Because it is an immediate recurrence corollary, the route conservatively assigns no novelty even without locating the identical displayed formula.

claim_boundary.allowed_wording: From the Amdeberhan--Zeilberger q-Apéry recurrence, the standard discrete Abel--Liouville identity yields an explicit nonzero Casoratian product for every real q>1; exact finite replay verifies the defining-sum specialization only for n=0 through 4.
forbidden_wording: The source paper proves the rational-base 3/2 result for all n.
Finite symbolic replay is an all-index proof.
Noncollapse proves irrationality or supplies small integer linear forms.
The opposite 2-adic and 3-adic valuations give simultaneous local gain.
The false uniform p-adic hypothesis (H) follows from the Casoratian.
